A1-A2.headline: The Big World Of American Football

pages.text: Get ready for the roar of the crowd! The National Football League is the top sports group in the United States. It started in 1920 with a different name. Today, 32 teams play in the league. They are split into two groups called conferences. The league office is in New York City.
pages.caption: Roger Goodell is the NFL commissioner.

evidence.articleCaption: Roger Goodell, National Football League Commissioner since 2006 (pictured in 2012)

pages.text: Every year, the season starts in August. Teams play 17 games in the regular season. After that, the best teams play in the playoffs. The final game is the Super Bowl. It is a very popular event for many people.

Each April, the league holds a draft. Teams pick new players from colleges. A team can have 55 players on its list, but only 48 can play on game day. This helps teams stay strong and fair for every season.
pages.caption: A player is picked in the draft.

evidence.articleCaption: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the first overall pick of the 2026 NFL draft

pages.text: The NFL is the richest sports league in the world. Many people watch the games on TV. It is the most popular sport in America. The league works hard to keep the games exciting for all the fans everywhere.

glossary.en_def: a period of time for sports

B1-B2.headline: Inside The Professional World Of American Football

pages.text: Feel the energy of the gridiron! The National Football League stands as the premier professional football organization in the United States. Established in 1920 as the American Professional Football Association, it rebranded in 1922. Today, the league consists of 32 teams divided into two conferences. Headquartered in New York, it manages the sport's growth.
pages.caption: Roger Goodell, NFL Commissioner since 2006.

evidence.articleCaption: Roger Goodell, National Football League Commissioner since 2006 (pictured in 2012)

pages.text: The annual schedule includes a preseason, an 18-week regular season, and a playoff tournament. Each team plays 17 games during the regular season. The season concludes with the Super Bowl, a major championship game. This tournament structure ensures that only the best teams compete for the title.

Every April, the NFL conducts a draft to select college players. Teams are limited to 55 players on their roster, with 48 active on game days. This system allows teams to refresh their talent annually, maintaining a competitive balance across the entire league throughout the year.
pages.caption: Fernando Mendoza, the 2026 NFL draft pick.

evidence.articleCaption: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the first overall pick of the 2026 NFL draft

pages.text: As the wealthiest professional sports league globally, the NFL enjoys immense popularity. Its games are among the most-watched television programs in the United States. By combining high-level competition with massive media reach, the league remains a dominant force in the world of professional sports today.

C1-C2.headline: The Evolution And Structure Of The National Football League

pages.text: Originating in 1920 as the American Professional Football Association, the National Football League has evolved into the preeminent professional football entity in the United States. Comprising 32 franchises partitioned into two conferences, the league operates from its New York City headquarters, overseeing a complex organizational structure that governs the sport.
pages.caption: Roger Goodell, NFL Commissioner since 2006.

evidence.articleCaption: Roger Goodell, National Football League Commissioner since 2006 (pictured in 2012)

pages.text: The competitive calendar is meticulously structured, featuring a brief preseason, an 18-week regular season, and a high-stakes, single-elimination playoff tournament. With each team playing 17 games, the season culminates in the Super Bowl. This format serves as the definitive mechanism for crowning the league's ultimate champion each February.

The annual draft, held every April, facilitates the integration of collegiate talent into the professional ranks. Clubs are restricted to a 55-player roster, with only 48 active on game days. This rigorous selection process is essential for maintaining competitive parity and ensuring the long-term sustainability of the league.
pages.caption: Fernando Mendoza, top 2026 NFL draft pick.

evidence.articleCaption: Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza, the first overall pick of the 2026 NFL draft

pages.text: Financially, the NFL stands as the most lucrative professional sports league globally. Its games consistently dominate American television ratings, cementing its status as a cultural and economic juggernaut. Through strategic media partnerships and a robust championship structure, the league maintains its unparalleled influence on the professional sports landscape.

glossary.en_def: a huge, powerful, and overwhelming force
